adapter: <scratch>/fresh/clique/repo/rsi6/environments/clique.py (manifest rsi6/environments/manifests/clique.json, data rsi6/data/clique/), maximum clique on the graphs of the second DIMACS challenge
statement: The clique adapter reads the DIMACS binary graph files correctly, and it reads the source's own statements of the maximum clique size correctly. The only thing it exposes is the relabelled adjacency matrix, and it scores exactly by the published objective. I wrote an independent parser from README.binformat. It reproduces the adapter's decoding: row i is padded to i//8+1 bytes and read high bit first. Read that way, the four Hamming and four Johnson graphs equal their definitions in contents.tex, and all 39 cliques the source publishes are cliques of exactly the reference size. My own reading of contents.tex, results.dmclique, results.dfmax, the solution files and the comment lines gives the same 56 instances, the same 56 reference values and the same 13 left out, with no conflicting statements. My independent evaluator agrees with the adapter on all 868 answers I generated (522 valid) and on all 5,574 partial-evaluation entries, with no exception. The reference cannot be observed through the problem object, and training and fresh problems are byte-identical. Relabelling is drawn per instance and per run seed, and it removes the answer information that the raw vertex order carries: in file order, the index-order maximal clique is maximum on the four Hamming graphs, two c-fat graphs and johnson8-4-4, but not after relabelling. Every malformed answer scores 0. All 104 pinned hashes reproduce, and the files I fetched again match. The references are the source's statements and were not re-proved here. For 8 of the 11 fresh brock graphs, the only support for the value in the source is the clique the generator built. What limits a result is headroom, not correctness. A greedy rule with no search scores 0.846 on the 24 fresh instances against a threshold of 0.90, and it reaches the reference on the 4 Hamming and 2 Johnson fresh graphs; the two Johnson graphs give a score of 1 to every maximal clique. On the confirming half (Hamming and p_hat graphs) the same rule scores 0.920, so a pass on that half is not evidence that anything was learned. The adapter's anchor says so, but nothing in the kernel's run record carries the warning. The owner must settle how that half is read in the registration before the category is used.
coverage:
Method: own scripts in <scratch>/fresh/clique/audit1 (hashes.py, preambles.py, own.py, structure.py, refs.py, check.py, split_anchor.py, last.py, listing.py; downloads in dl/). own.py shares no code with the adapter. It has its own decoder, written from README.binformat, which I tested under both bit orders and two row layouts. It has its own readers for contents.tex, results.dmclique, results.dfmax, the solution files and the comment lines, and its own evaluator and scorer (Fraction arithmetic).

Checked:
(1) I read every line of clique.py. There is no search, ranking, pruning or optimisation call. The precomputed `apart` matrix only serves exact evaluation.
(2) I set the stored reference to ref, 2, ref+1 and 1e6 on 12 instances, with training=True and False. The pickled public view fields, the adapter attributes, the candidates() and evaluate() outputs and the meter usage were byte-identical in every case. The reference value occurs in no attribute, private ones included.
(3) Two run seeds give different orders on all 56 instances, and two 300-vertex instances under one run seed are relabelled differently. decode() inverts the permutation exactly. The 39 published cliques, given under 3 relabellings, all score 1 and evaluate to [-ref, 0]. A first-ref or last-ref block is never a clique after relabelling. The raw-order index greedy reaches the maximum on c-fat200-1, c-fat500-1, hamming6-2, 6-4, 8-2, 8-4 and johnson8-4-4; relabelled, it falls to the random-order level (mean 0.643 vs 0.648).
(4) Evaluator agreement: see that field.
(5) Degenerate answers, all scoring 0: empty, all ones, one vertex, two non-adjacent vertices, values 2 and -1, float 0/1, NaN, bool, short, 2-D, list, None, object dtype. A uint8 edge is accepted. Sub-cliques k = 0..ref of every published clique score exactly max(0, (k-1)/(ref-1)), strictly increasing up to ref.
(6) I ran split(env, 16, 24) from rsi6.kernel.environment, and halves(), layout() and _valid() from rsi6.kernel.run (import allowed for these only; it pulls in rsi6.learner.designs at import, but nothing of the learner was called). Results: one layout across all 56 problems under both training flags; the view's state keys are {a, used, tot, n} and var_var is read-only; no train/fresh pair has equal (n, m) or an equal degree sequence.
(7) I replicated the anchor's two rules (20 random orders, 5 greedy runs).
(8) All 104 pinned hashes recomputed, with no unlisted file on disk. I fetched these again and their hashes match the pins: contents.tex, results.dmclique, brock800_4.clq.b, c-fat500-10.sol. The volume copies of p_hat300-1, brock200_2, keller5 and MANN_a27 are byte-identical to the pinned benchmark files. I read the 7 directory listings and the unpinned text files (contents.tex.BAK, LAST_UPDATEAug15/Sep20, README.nmclique, san2.sol, NEW_FILES, NOV2893.UPD, SEP1993.UPD): none states a clique size that differs, and no page states a licence or terms. Listing dates: p_hat files corrected 1993-09-23, results.dfmax and results.dmclique dated 1993-09-27 (after the correction); all 12 p_hat files carry the correction note. Metering: start 1, candidates 2 per variable, assign 1, evaluate n. No clique larger than a reference was found by 30 random-order and 3 greedy runs per instance.

Not checked:
- The optimality of any reference (not attempted, per the rules).
- 12 of the 16 volume copies.
- Graph definitions of keller, c-fat, MANN, brock, p_hat and san; only Hamming and Johnson were re-derived, though the 39 published cliques test the decoding across families.
- Process claims ("fixed before anything was scored", "knowing no learner result").
- The learner-dependent generic tests (not run, as required).

Conduct: total CPU about 10 s. Nothing under the repo copy was written: no __pycache__, and find -newer printed nothing. Note that those two find commands traversed every subdirectory of the repo copy, though they printed nothing.
exposed:
The problem object (seen through AssignView) exposes:
- var_var[0]: an n×n float matrix of 0/1, the graph's adjacency relabelled by the seed's permutation. It traces to the binary block of the .clq.b file: bit j of row i in the lower triangle, rows padded to i//8+1 bytes, high bit first, symmetrised, diagonal 0. It equals my own decode relabelled by the permutation decode() implies, on all 56 instances.
- n_vars = NODES of the file's p line; n_opts = 2 (the answer form: 0 out, 1 in).
- hard = [False, True], detail = [False, False]. These are the two spec-defined groups: [0] minus the number of vertices chosen; [1] the number of chosen pairs not joined by an edge (0 exactly for a clique).
- var_attr (n,0) and opt_attr (2,0): empty. opt_opt, var_opt, occ_attr: empty tuples. capacity, domain, start_answer, start_totals: None. ordered: False.
- candidates(), evaluate() and totals() return only exact changes and totals of those two groups.

Behind the view and never exposed: adjacent and apart, both relabelled, on the problem object. On the environment, kernel only: the references, claims and left_out.

Design decisions that shape difficulty, said plainly:
- Group [1] counts conflicting pairs rather than flagging validity. So candidates() tells, for every vertex, how many current members it is not adjacent to, which gives the candidate set of a greedy construction. That is exact evaluation of the stated terms, not a heuristic.
- No vertex attribute is exposed, not even the degree; a learner must derive everything from var_var.
- Variables cannot be reassigned, so the form admits constructions but not moves.
- The score's zero point is one vertex. A random maximal clique therefore already scores about 0.6, and the greedy rule about 0.85.
evaluator_agreement:
Answers compared: 868, on 31 instances (every second instance, plus hamming8-2, MANN_a27 and keller5), all generated in the relabelled problem. 522 were valid: random maximal cliques built from var_var, and random sub-cliques of them, the empty set included. 346 were invalid random vertex sets. Each answer went through the adapter's score(decode(answer)), the problem's evaluate() and my own validity, score and totals computed on my own decode. There were 0 disagreements in score, in totals [-k, non-adjacent pairs], or in validity (hard group 0 exactly for cliques).

Partial evaluation: 5,574 candidate entries, over unassigned and already-assigned variables and both options, on 7 instances along random partial assignments. Every entry equals the difference of my own partial totals, the fast rows equal AssignProblem._rows at every step, and totals() after assign() equals partial_totals() and my own totals.

References: I parsed all 56 independently from the pinned files, and they equal the adapter's.
- Statements per source among the 56: [OPT = k] for 50, table 32, dfmax 28, solution file 25, comment line 18. No two disagree, and no lower bound exceeds a value.
- The source publishes answers for 39 instances: 25 solution files (numbered from 0), 12 brock comment lists (from 0) and 2 MANN lists (from 1). Each is a clique of exactly the reference size under my parser, not under the other numbering, and each scores 1.
- For the other 17 (5 gen, 7 san, sanr400_0.5, johnson32-2-4, keller5, p_hat700-1, p_hat1000-1) the source publishes values only. For all of these except the gen graphs, results.dmclique's frequency tables show the reference size was reached.

findings.title: The confirming half is passed by a rule with no learning
findings.problem: halves() puts the Ham and PHat groups (11 instances) in the confirming half. There a greedy rule with no search and no learning already scores 0.920, above the threshold of 0.90. A pass on that half is therefore not evidence of acquisition, for any learner whose construction is about as good as greedy. On the whole fresh set the same rule scores 0.846, only 0.054 below the threshold, and it reaches the reference on 6 of the 24 instances in every run. The adapter states this in its anchor and docstring. But the run record carries only the number 0.90, and nothing in the kernel stops a pass on that half being read as a confirmation.
findings.evidence: split_anchor.py printed: 'half A: 13 [Bro, Joh] | half B: 11 [Ham, PHat]'; 'greedy: all 56 0.83 fresh 24 0.846'; 'greedy: half A 0.783 half B 0.92'; 'fresh Ham: greedy 1.0 ... greedy==1 on all runs: [hamming8-2, hamming8-4, hamming6-4, hamming6-2]'; 'fresh PHat: greedy 0.875'. These match the anchor's 0.845 and 0.918 within sampling noise.
findings.fix: Before clique enters a registered run, the owner states in the registration how this half is read. One option: a pass there must exceed the untrained score by a stated margin. Another: threshold_for(ids) returns a separate value for exactly those 11 ids, set above the greedy rule's 0.92 and stated in the anchor. Otherwise, do not use clique where an independent confirming half is required. The scoring code needs no change.

findings.title: The two fresh Johnson graphs score 1 for every maximal clique (not stated)
findings.problem: johnson8-2-4 and johnson16-2-4 are both fresh and both in the deciding half. Their cliques are sets of pairwise disjoint 2-subsets of an even ground set, so every maximal clique is a perfect matching of reference size, and any construction that ends on a maximal clique scores 1.0. The docstring says only that the greedy rule reaches the maximum there. So 2 of the 13 deciding instances carry no signal at all. To reach 0.90 on that half, the 11 brock graphs must average about 0.882, against the greedy rule's 0.743.
findings.evidence: split_anchor.py printed 'fresh Joh: greedy 1.0 random 1.0' (20 random maximal cliques each). structure.py confirmed both graphs equal the contents.tex definition: weight-2 vectors adjacent iff hamming distance >= 4, i.e. disjoint supports.
findings.fix: In the docstring's 'What the fresh instances can show' and in the anchor, add: the two drawn Johnson graphs give 1 to every maximal clique, the four Hamming graphs give 1 to the greedy rule, and the decision on the deciding half rests on the 11 brock graphs.

findings.title: The docstring's quoted evidence for the SanR family also fits san1000, and the quote is altered
findings.problem: The docstring cites the sanr files' comment line as evidence that they form their own family. But san1000.clq.b, which the adapter keeps in San with reference 15, carries the identical DESCRIPTION line. The quote also silently corrects the source's spelling ('differenct') inside quotation marks. Keeping san1000 in San is still well supported: the table codes it (San), its parameter line has the san form ('c 1000 249000 985 1499 40473 7', where sanr has 'c 200 0.300000 3769'), and it states '15 max clique'. San and SanR are both on the training side, so the split is unaffected.
findings.evidence: preambles.py full san1000 printed 'c DESCRIPTION:  Randomly generated graph of similar size to "san" / c               graphs, but with differenct clique characteristics', followed by 'c 1000 vertices 250500 edges 15 max clique'.
findings.fix: Amend the paragraph 'Groups of instances': quote the source's wording exactly, and say that san1000 carries the same DESCRIPTION line but stays in San because of its table code, its san-type parameter line and its stated maximum.
